questions.evidence:
In a classroom demonstration, Bao places a printed letter on the desk and looks at it through a handheld magnifier. At one position, the letter appears larger. He sketches what he sees, then moves the lens slightly and notices that the view changes.

The teacher asks whether the printed letter itself has grown. Bao measures its height with a ruler after setting the lens aside. The ink still occupies the same space on the page. What changed was the view through the lens, not the physical size of the printing.

The class records the lens position for each drawing. Students try to keep the page and their viewing position steady while changing the lens distance. They describe the image before offering an explanation, and they do not use a drawing as a direct measurement of the ink.

Bao adds two labels to his notes: object and observed image. The distinction helps him explain why a larger-looking letter does not require a larger printed page. Careful observation includes recognizing what the tool changes about the way something is seen.
questions.explanation: 有鏡視圖與直接量測對照才能區分。
